newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Focus - Ericsson share calms, future shaky.
newsitem.headline: Focus - Ericsson share calms, future shaky.

text.p: Shares in Swedish telecoms group Ericsson stabilised following a sharp fall on Monday but analysts said the share's short-term direction was uncertain.
At 1140 GMT the share was trading at 235.5 crowns, a fall of 14 crowns or 5.6 percent from Friday's close. The share was off a low of 231.5 it hit at the Monday opening in Stockholm.

The slide mirrored a fall in New York on Friday to the eqvivalent of 231 crowns in New York after closing at 249.5 in Stockholm on the day the company posted a 30 percent rise in first quarter pre-tax profit to 2.02 billion crowns.
"The price fall in New York on Friday is absolutely an overreaction," said Susan Anthony, an analyst at Schroeders.
"The result was good, but not in line with the highest forecasts and that was necessary for the share to increase," she added.
Ericsson's result on Friday, which for the first time allowed a breakdown between its mobile handsets and mobile systems performance profit, was overall slightly higher than the market had expected.
The company highlighted the role of mobile handsets which had 100 percent sales growth, and said it had gained market share.
But Ericsson put in mobile systems growth of 22 percent, which some analysts found below expectations and which was cited as a reason behind its sharp fall in New York and Stockholm.
Swedbank analyst Ulf Hellzen was one of the analysts who said investors were reacting to developments within the Mobile System unit.
"Mobile System was not as strong as expected and the negative cash flow has worried the market," Hellzen said.
He added that it was difficult to tell which way the share would move in the short-term.

"The share had been traded up ahead of the report on high expectations and I think it has levelled out now. I think that it has reached a correct level but it is difficult to say which way it will go in the short-term," Hellzen said.
The share was, however, trading ex-dividend with 2.50 crowns taken from its price, some dealers pointed out.

"This is still higher than the closing level in New York...and considering the dividend I don't think we should worry too much," a dealer said. "Both the buy and the sell side are active and there is no shortage of buyers."
Anthony said the share would probably not fall much further but said it probably would not rise significantly.
"I don't think the share will make any big jumps in the coming months ahead of the next financial report," she said.
Others said the market needed time to see the effects of changes in accounting and company restructuring.
"It's a little like drug company Astra. The market would like to have another quarter in order to see a significant trend," said one head dealer.

A Reuters survey showed that analysts expect Ericsson's Finnish rival Nokia Oy to post a 1.26 million markka 1997 profit before tax and minority interest on average, sharply up from 399 million in the year-ago period. That result is due on April 29.

Nokia, which as Europe's number one in handset sales is growing from a much larger base, is not expected to put in as glitzy a growth figure as Ericsson's 100 percent when it reports on Tuesday, partly because it has a larger analog share.
